note: mapping_basis=data_labels: the .do keeps REG12A's own columns P1205A-P1205C and sets item = the source column name (core model s3 pattern 1, no rename). The data dictionary's variable labels tie P1205A..C to the questionnaire's rows in order ('a. Ley 1600, Contra la violencia doméstica' = P1205A, 'b. Ley 4788, Integral contra la trata de personas' = P1205B, 'c. Ley 5777, De protección integral a las mujeres, contra toda forma de violencia' = P1205C), 3/3. Row 'otra, especificar' (P1205D, 'd. Otros', raw Sí/No/NR 27/2630/1) is not kept by the .do and is not in this table. RESP: the .do (Bookmark 3) sets 9 (NR) to missing and recodes (6=1)(1=2), so source 1 Sí / 6 No becomes live 1 = No, 2 = Sí; option_text is keyed to the LIVE codes (1 No, 2 Sí). Route 9: raw REG12A counts recoded equal live resp 1/2 in 6/6 item x resp cells; the unrecoded reading matches 0/6. Live 1/2 (= raw No/Sí): P1205A 1483/1175, P1205B 1889/766, P1205C 1691/967. FILTER: 1205 is asked only if 1204 ('¿Sabe que existen leyes que protegen los derechos de la mujer?') = Sí; raw P1204 Sí/No/NR = 2657/618/1, and the 617 other P1204=No women are blank on 1205. One woman (UPM 28084, NVIVI 33, NHOGA 1) has P1204 = No yet P1205A-C = No (skip-pattern inconsistency in INE's file); she is in the live table with resp 1 on all three. The P1204=NR woman is NR (9) on every 1205 row and is dropped. Dropped NR (9): P1205A 1, P1205B 4, P1205C 1. Live 7971 rows = 2658 x 3 - 3 (the .do asserts 7971), 2658 ids. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (3 items, resp {1,2}). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the questionnaire's 1205 stem '¿Conoce alguna de las leyes de protección de los derechos de la mujer, como...' joined to each row's text with its dot leaders and the line-wraps dropped (same stem+row convention as batch_601-603). The stem has no closing '?' in the questionnaire, the manual or the dictionary and none is added. The questionnaire's curly quotes around the law titles are kept; the dictionary prints them as '?' (encoding loss) and prefixes row letters a.-c. which the questionnaire does not print, so the questionnaire is shipped. The manual gives the stem as 'como…' (single ellipsis character); the questionnaire's '...' is shipped. instructions left blank: no read-aloud framing precedes 1205; 1204 is a separate filter question not in the table, and the manual's 'ENCUESTADORA: LEA LAS OPCIONES A LA ENTREVISTADA Y MARQUE TODAS LAS QUE ELLA MENCIONE' is an interviewer direction. option_text = the questionnaire's column headers verbatim (Sí, No; dictionary agrees); no row for NR 9. Single section_id, no section_prompt. language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation: INE publishes the ENSIMUP in Spanish only; all English produced by IRW ('Integral contra la trata de personas' rendered 'Comprehensive law against trafficking in persons', the word 'law' supplied; 'De protección integral' 'On the comprehensive protection'). Issues-page entry owed once live. STEP 3b: dictionary Description ('Knowledge of specific Paraguayan laws protecting women against domestic violence, trafficking, and all forms of violence') matches 1205's three named laws exactly; 3 live items = 3 named-law rows; 2-level resp = Sí/No. RIGHTS: originator INE Paraguay; the questionnaire and manual cite no upstream instrument for 1204/1205. public_note: The English wording for this table was produced by IRW, not by INE Paraguay, which publishes the ENSIMUP 2021 in Spanish only; these questions were asked only of women who first said they knew that laws protecting women's rights exist (question 1204); and the response codes were reversed in processing so that 1 = No and 2 = Sí (yes), unlike the questionnaire's 1 = Sí, 6 = No.
